actors.notes: Demonstrated PEAK capability of current frontier models wielded as autonomous/agentic operators (GTG-1002, Claude Mythos Preview, OpenAI 5.3-Codex, AISLE, ARTEMIS). The standout uplift is server-side vulnerability discovery and exploit development (#2=Champion): AISLE independently found all 12 zero-days in the Jan-2026 OpenSSL release (some missed by decades of fuzzing/audit); Claude Mythos found thousands of high/critical vulns incl. decades-old zero-days; OpenAI 5.3-Codex was first to formally hit the 'High' cyber threshold (working remote zero-day exploits vs. well-defended systems); ARTEMIS outperformed 9/10 human pros across ~8,000 hosts. Malware authoring is mature and ubiquitous (#7=Champion). Post-compromise abuse of legitimate functions/LOTL, backdoor creation, and discovery are strong (#1=High). Credential harvesting + reuse is High (#4) but bounded by occasional credential hallucination — still an obstacle to FULL autonomy. Social engineering capability is high (deepfakes, hyper-personalized phishing, autonomous conversational agents) but observed malicious use is shifting deeper into the chain (#9=High). Supply-chain compromise (dependency/package poisoning at scale, e.g. Shai-Hulud-class worms) is rising (#10=High). NO meaningful AI uplift for Man-in-the-Middle (#5), Flooding/DDoS (#6, a botnet/resource game), or Physical (#8) — these stay Low and keep the radar honest rather than uniformly inflated. In GTG-1002 the model executed 80-90% of the operation autonomously at thousands of requests/sec, with humans intervening at only 4-6 decision points.

actors.notes: The TYPICAL real-world picture of AI-assisted malicious users, derived from Anthropic's study of 832 accounts banned for cyber misuse (Mar 2025-Mar 2026), rather than the frontier ceiling. Malware writing is the single most common AI-assisted activity (560/832 = 67.3%), so #7=High. Social-engineering content generation remains a strong uplift at scale (#9=High), though AI-assisted phishing actually DECLINED 8.6% in the dataset as actors shifted effort deeper into the chain. Post-compromise uses grew: account/network discovery +8.9%, lateral movement 54/832 = 6.5% (#1=Medium). Most exploitation and credential work is AI-assisted rather than AI-led, so #2/#3/#4=Medium. The proportion of medium/high-risk actors using AI jumped from 33% to 56% (1.7x) across the year — AI raises the floor broadly even where it doesn't reach frontier autonomy. No uplift for MitM (#5), Flooding (#6), or Physical (#8).
sources: Anthropic, 'What we learned mapping a year's worth of AI-enabled cyber threats' (832 banned accounts mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, Mar 2025-Mar 2026), Jun 2026
